cells.tense: You are moving and you are saying where the line is as you cross it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have already decided and say it out loud before you touch it again.
cells.core:
You can tell when a thing in your way is nothing, and you go through it without waiting for permission. You say the boundary by walking it. Nothing grand about it — you move, the shape of the room changes, you keep going.

What keeps this clean is that you are still listening while you move. You test your own reading of the ground, and when the test comes back empty you change tack without calling it a loss. Tomorrow: pick one thing you have already decided and say it out loud before you touch it again. The deciding stays with you, and the ground stays fresh.

cells.place: a room where a wall has just come down and the shape of the space is suddenly plain

cells.tense: You are charging at a shape that has not arrived and treating it as already in your way.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are running at and leave it alone for a day, then say what still stands.
cells.core:
You are ahead of the moment. Something might need clearing soon, so you have already charged at it — the talk you have not had, the call nobody asked you to make, a wall that may not be there. The push is real. So is what it takes out of you.

You do not have to stop being the one who moves. Pick one thing you are running at and leave it alone for a day, then say what still stands. What is actually false will still be false tomorrow. What is real gets a day to show you its size, and you can spend your weight on that instead of on the guess.

cells.tense: A wall came down and you have been standing at the gap taking its measure.
cells.ask: Put one small irreversible change into the room this week and let the result sit.
cells.core:
The wall came down and you have not stepped through. You can see the gap. You are watching it, measuring it, and the moving stopped before it reached anything. Standing there costs nothing obvious. It is not rest.

It does not need a loud return. Put one small irreversible change into the room this week and let the result sit — a cleared corner, a habit ended, a thing said once and not argued. Small is enough. Passing through a false structure is how it finishes coming down, and one changed thing carries you through. You do not have to feel ready to make one thing in the room different.

cells.tense: You are already clearing the ground and you keep describing it as the situation.
cells.ask: Say 'I made that change' about one thing you have been calling inevitable or somebody else's call.
cells.core:
Things have already moved because you moved them. The relationship that ended, the plan that changed, the false thing that got dropped — you are the one who dropped it, and you tell it as if it grew on its own. The clearing is done. The hand that did it is still out of the frame.

Nobody outside you needs to hear this. Say 'I made that change' about one thing you have been calling inevitable or somebody else's call. It is not a claim about whether the change was right. It is just the doing coming back to the doer. From there the next clearing is a choice and not a forecast.
cells.sheetLine: The ground was cleared by you, and you are telling it otherwise.

The ask survives my being wrong because offering a testable piece of authority is useful even if their balance is not what I read.
